name: Auxiliary Cost of Cartesian Powers
statement: For every nonempty proper maximum-generated $C$, the limit $\gamma(C)=\lim_{k\to\infty}a(C^k)/k=\inf_{k\ge1}b(C^k)/k$ exists and $\operatorname{VC}(C)\le\gamma(C)\le b(C)$. Visible constant coordinates do not change $\gamma$. If $d=\operatorname{VC}(C)$ and $C$ has a rank-$d$ parent with at most $d$ auxiliaries, then $b(C^k)=kd$, $kd-m(C)\le a(C^k)\le kd$, and $\gamma(C)=d$. In particular a proper rank-$d$ maximum class satisfies $(k-1)d\le a(M^k)\le kd$ and $b(M^k)=kd$.
proof: The sequence $b(C^k)$ is subadditive, so the elementary subadditive-limit argument gives its normalized limit and infimum formula. Product cores satisfy $m(C^k)=m(C)$ and $0\le b(C^k)-a(C^k)\le m(C)$, hence the normalized $a$-sequence has the same limit. Parent rank is at least $k\operatorname{VC}(C)$, yielding the lower bound; subadditivity yields the upper bound. Under the stated certificate, both bounds force $b(C^k)=kd$. Constant invariance follows because $(C\times\{0\}^t)^k$ is a constant extension of $C^k$.
